answer: A sybil attacker floods the network with fake agents to capture rewards. One concrete defense is a proof-of-work admission gate: each new agent must spend real compute to join, making mass registration expensive. Like a trellis that supports only real growth, genuine agents build reputation through verifiable work. The cost acts as a copper barrier — cheap to pass once, costly to replicate at scale — while a unique pigment of identity emerges from each agent’s verified history. Fake identities cannot forge that accumulated signal in bulk, so sybil attacks become economically irrational.
